gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the FranklinWH aPower 2 has no solar (PV/MPPT) input. It is an AC-coupled battery that needs a separate solar inverter, so FranklinWH's actual all-in-one unit is the aPower S, which has 4 built-in MPPTs and takes up to 20 kW of panels directly.
standout_why: I compared the three cited rivals. EnergySage (energysage.com/energy-storage/best-batteries-for-whole-home-backup) labels aPower 2 'AC' and says it 'works with almost any existing inverter setup', but never says the box has no solar input. iTechGuides (itechguides.com/tesla-powerwall-alternatives...) lists aPower 2 as 'AC coupled' and explicitly leaves the solar inverter as not stated. SolutionEnergy (solutionenergy.com/batteries/) says aPower 2 stores energy 'from solar, grid, generator, and EV' but says nothing about inverters or coupling. None of the three names the aPower S. All three already say Powerwall 3 has a built-in solar inverter, so that part is not new. iTechGuides already says EG4 PowerPro 'requires a compatible EG4 hybrid inverter'.
decides: The shopper asked for an all-in-one inverter and battery. ChatGPT's #4 pick, aPower 2, does not meet that: a solar buyer still needs a separate PV inverter (aPower S datasheets also show an aGate in the system). The correct FranklinWH single-box option is the aPower S. That leaves Powerwall 3 and aPower S as the only single-enclosure PV+battery picks among these brands. The EG4 route (FlexBOSS21 hybrid inverter with 3 MPPTs and 21 kW usable PV, plus a separate 48 V battery) is two boxes, which ChatGPT already noted. This confirms Powerwall 3 as best overall and replaces aPower 2 with aPower S for anyone who wants FranklinWH's 15 kWh per unit.

findings.label: Coupling / solar input
findings.value: AC-coupled; FranklinWH's spec table has no PV/MPPT input section; 'compatible with any solar inverter'
findings.source_title: Components of Franklin Home Power | FranklinWH Support
findings.note: The maker's spec table lists 'AC-coupled' for aPower 2 and gives an MPPT count and solar STC input only for aPower S. The conclusion that a separate solar inverter is needed is my inference from the missing PV input and the 'compatible with any solar inverter' wording. The page does not state it outright.

findings.label: Integrated solar inverter
findings.value: 4 MPPTs, 15 A per MPPT, maximum solar STC input 20 kW; 'battery storage device with integrated inverters to support a direct connection to solar (PV) panels'
findings.source_title: Components of Franklin Home Power | FranklinWH Support
findings.note: Same maker page. It also says aPower S 'supports parallel AC-coupled connection with FranklinWH aPower 2 batteries'.

findings.label: Capacity / PV / charge power
findings.value: 15 kWh per unit; 'A single aPower S unit can access 20 kW solar panels'; up to 8 kW charging power
findings.note: The product page says aPower S 'integrates formerly external inverter with battery storage into a single unit'. No price is shown.

findings.label: Continuous output with PV
findings.source_title: Meet aPower S: the Next-Generation Home Battery with Direct Solar Integration (FranklinWH blog, 2025-10-14)
findings.note: The maker's launch post. It describes PCS 'integrated directly into the battery' and says aPower S is backwards compatible with earlier aPower units via AC coupling.

findings.label: Integrated solar inputs (US version)
findings.value: Up to 20 kW of solar via 6 MPPTs at 13 A each (two can be paralleled to 26 A); 13.5 kWh; 11.5 kW continuous
findings.source_title: Tesla Powerwall 3 Review – Clean Energy Reviews (Jason Svarc, updated Nov 2024)
findings.note: Tesla.com returned 403 and the Tesla datasheet PDFs did not extract as text, so this is the named reviewer. Search excerpts of newer Tesla datasheets suggest a revision to 3 MPPTs at 26 A, so the MPPT layout may have changed. The 20 kW PV figure is the same in both.

findings.label: Limits at time of review
findings.value: Battery charge power limited to 5 kW; 'not (yet) certified for off-grid use'; needs Gateway 2 (or the US Backup Switch) for backup
findings.source_title: Tesla Powerwall 3 Review – Clean Energy Reviews (Jason Svarc, updated Nov 2024)
findings.note: Jason Svarc, Clean Energy Reviews, Nov 2024. Tesla firmware or certification may have changed since. The review also says Powerwall 2 'is an AC battery that needs to be installed with a separate solar inverter', the same split as aPower 2 vs aPower S.

findings.label: Hybrid inverter PV and output (battery separate)
findings.value: 3 integrated MPPTs; 21 kW usable PV (24,000 W maximum paired solar); 12,000 W battery-only / 16,000 W PV+battery continuous; 48 V battery input; UL1741
findings.source_title: EG4® FlexBOSS21 Inverter | Briggs & Stratton Energy Solutions
findings.note: Spec table on the Briggs & Stratton energy product page (eg4electronics.com product URL returned 404). It lists battery compatibility separately, so the inverter and battery are two products.
